item.title: ‘Know the law, own your power’: Atlanta town hall focuses on voting rights and civic action
item.description: The Links, Incorporated hosted a town hall to examine the potential impact of the upcoming U.S. Supreme Court case Louisiana v. Callais on minority political power, and to encourage students to view civic participation as ongoing work. item.title: The Silent Killer of Black Maternal Health
item.description: Obria Smith, a 31-year-old Atlanta native, tragically passed away from complications of eclampsia, a condition that disproportionately affects African American women and is running rampant in the US, with cases of pre-eclampsia rising 25% between 1987 and 2004. The post The Silent Killer of Black Maternal Health appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: Atlanta United preseason opener might be a sign of things to come
item.description: Atlanta United began their 2026 preseason with a 4-0 victory over Lexington SC, with manager Gerardo "Tata" Martino praising the team's performance and the individual play of several players. item.title: AUC Students March to the Capitol in nonviolent protests to ICE policies
item.description: Students from Clark Atlanta University, Morris Brown College, Morehouse College, and Spelman College marched from the Atlanta University Center to the Georgia State Capitol to protest immigration policies, state-sanctioned violence, and policies that harm the Black community. The post AUC Students March to the Capitol in nonviolent protests to ICE policies appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.description: Gallery Anderson Smith celebrated its grand re-opening in West Midtown, offering a unique atmosphere and experience for Atlanta's art crowd, with the goal of creating a space for both established and emerging artists to showcase their work. item.title: Grammy Awards 2026: See which nominees took home golden gramophones
item.description: Bad Bunny made history at the Grammy Awards by becoming the first Spanish-language artist to win album of the year, while Kendrick Lamar broke the record for the most awarded rapper in Grammys history, and Billie Eilish made a political statement about ICE while accepting her award. item.title: Atlanta Braves are headed south for spring training, new promo items on tap for 2026 season
item.description: The Atlanta Braves loaded up trucks with gear for spring training on Monday, February 2, and also previewed some of the promotional giveaways scheduled for the 2026 season, including a replica Dale Murphy jersey, bobbleheads of former Braves players, and the new "Crossover Collection" of jerseys. The post Atlanta Braves are headed south for spring training, new promo items on tap for 2026 season appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: The Devil Is Busy: Spelman College screens Oscar-Nominated short on abortion access
item.description: Spelman College hosted a screening of the HBO documentary short "The Devil Is Busy" followed by a Q&A with director Christalyn Hampton and executive producer Soledad O'Brien, which follows Tracii, the head of security at Feminist Women's Health Center in Atlanta, as she navigates the daily reality of the clinic amidst legal restrictions and protests. The post The Devil Is Busy: Spelman College screens Oscar-Nominated short on abortion access appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: Georgia Senate Public Safety Committee holds Anti-squatting Act hearing
item.description: House Bill 61, known as the "Georgia Anti-Squatting Act of 2026", aims to hasten the removal of unauthorized occupants from residential properties, hotels, and cars, allowing immediate lockouts and treating nonpayment as criminal trespass, which housing rights advocates argue could harm low-income, long-term residents in extended-stay hotels. The post Georgia Senate Public Safety Committee holds Anti-squatting Act hearing appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.
